newsitem.title: CANADA: BC Tel, Simmonds units in TV deal.
newsitem.headline: BC Tel, Simmonds units in TV deal.

text.p: Subsidiaries of BC Telecom Inc and Simmonds Capital Ltd said Thursday they formed a joint venture to pursue opportunities in wireless digital television and high-speed Internet access in British Columbia.

The effort is aimed at bringing "consumers a powerful alternative to cable television," BC TEL Interactive and PowerTel TV said. PowerTel described itself as a leader in Canada's emerging wireless digital television industry.
Under the proposed venture, the new services would be delivered to consumers through multichannel multipoint distribution systems (MMDS), a wireless digital technology.

"MMDS can deliver higher quality television and better value than cable -- thanks to digital pictures and sound, a 100-channel programming line-up, and the ability to offer a range of Internet applications. And without an expensive cable or satellite infrastructure, MMDS services can offer this outstanding package at very competitive prices," the two companies said.

The joint venture is subject to the final approval of the boards of both companies. All proposed broadcast services would also be subject to approval of the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) and Industry Canada.
The companies gave no financial details or prospective launch dates for the service.
